title: Root Cellars, Home Butchering and Fireless Cooking (Historical)

attribution: Adapted from U.S. Department of Agriculture Farmers' Bulletins 1939, Home Storage of Vegetables and Fruits (revised 1960); 1186, Pork on the Farm (1921); 1415, Beef on the Farm (1924); and 771, Homemade Fireless Cookers and Their Use (1916), from National Agricultural Library scans at the Internet Archive; selected sections only. Reformatted into sections without changing substance; figures not included; scanning (OCR) errors are left as found. Use does not imply endorsement by USDA or the U.S. Government.
description: Storing vegetables and fruits in cellars and pits (1960), slaughtering and cutting hogs and cattle (1921, 1924), and homemade fireless cookers (1916); the bulletins' curing, canning and fumigation instructions are left out as unsafe. Food in a fireless cooker cools for hours and can fall into the 40–140°F danger zone where bacteria multiply, and the 1916 bulletin recommends asbestos insulation — do not follow it as current advice.
